set.body:
Phase G (ergonomics). Must follow Phase D — see ordering note below.

Problem: the flagship typed-task guide opens with partial-function unwrapping. docs/examples/typed-task.md:15-18:

    OperationId.from("example.increment").toOption.get,
    OperationVersion.from("1").toOption.get,
    SchemaId.from("example.int-input.v1").toOption.get,
    ResultSchemaId.from("example.int-result.v1").toOption.get

Four consecutive .toOption.get calls, then handwritten codecs, a registry and attachment plumbing — before the reader has run anything. The same pattern recurs throughout the test suite (e.g. SlurmParsersSuite.scala:266-283), so the docs teach the idiom the codebase practices.

This directly contradicts docs/plans/2026-07-23-site-layer.md:47-49, which commits to "inline literal constructors (compile-time scala.compiletime.error) so no fold(throw) ceremony". Either they were never built or they are unused.

Two-surface design:
- an explicit substrate for infrastructure authors;
- a compact, safe Job surface with named products and literal interpolators.

Dynamic values still return Either/ValidatedNec; LITERALS check at compile time. A large fluent builder DSL is unnecessary and is explicitly not the goal.

ORDERING (the review's own point, and it is right): this must come after P8.D1/D2. Otherwise the friendly surface stabilizes exactly the concepts the launch/result split is about to change, and the ergonomic layer has to be designed twice.
set.title: P8.G1: Compact Job surface and literal constructors
